questions.question: Day 5 Scenario (Customer Escalations & Quality): Select the natural English phrasing when My sister is checking grocery item stock this evening:

options.a: Milk packet no stock having. yesterday
options.b: I am checking grocery item stock right now.
options.c: Milk packet no stock having.
options.d: Fresh milk packets were completely out of stock.

questions.explanation:

Natural everyday English uses standard tense agreement: "Fresh milk packets were completely out of stock.".

questions.question: Day 5 Vocabulary (Customer Escalations & Quality): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'pick out'?

options.a: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.
options.b: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.
options.c: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.
options.d: Carefully choose specific items from a group.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
'pick out' means: carefully choose specific items from a group. Example: "Could you help me pick out the best mangos?"

questions.question:
Day 5 Translation Scenario 1 (Customer Escalations & Quality):

Telugu: "నేను సాధారణంగా ఉదయం 6 గంటలకే నిద్రలేచి ఒక కప్పు టీ తాగుతాను."
(Literal attempt: "I generally in morning 6 clock wake up drink tea.")

options.a: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.b: I am needing to i generally in morning 6 clock wake up drink tea.
options.c: I generally in morning 6 clock wake up drink tea.
options.d: I usually wake up at 6:00 AM and have a cup of tea.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
Natural Version: "I usually wake up at 6:00 AM and have a cup of tea."

Use 'have a cup of tea' and specify time as '6:00 AM'.

questions.question:
Day 5 Translation Scenario 2 (Customer Escalations & Quality):

Telugu: "నా పార్సెల్ ఈ రోజు సాయంత్రానికి డెలివరీ అవుతుందా?"
(Literal attempt: "My parcel today evening delivery becoming?")

options.a: My parcel today evening delivery becoming?
options.b: I am needing to my parcel today evening delivery becoming?
options.c: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.d: Will my package be delivered by this evening?

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
Natural Version: "Will my package be delivered by this evening?"

Use 'Will my package be delivered...' for delivery tracking.

(Literal attempt: "To me little headache is there, take rest one hour.")

options.a: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.b: To me little headache is there, take rest one hour.
options.c: I am needing to to me little headache is there, take rest one hour.
options.d: I have a slight headache; I'm going to rest for an hour.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
Natural Version: "I have a slight headache; I'm going to rest for an hour."

Say 'I have a slight headache' instead of literal translations.
